cells.statement: A substance can be classified by the question asked of it: what it basically is, what molecular framework it has, what role it plays in living systems, what practical use it serves, or which field of study frames it.
cells.name: A substance can be classified by the question asked of it: what it basically is, what molecular framework it has, what role it plays in living systems, what practical use it serves, or which field of study frames it.

points.statement: General chemical categories name what a substance is at the most basic level, from broad chemical entity down to the single atom.
points.name: General chemical categories name what a substance is at the most basic level, from broad chemical entity down to the single atom.

support.rank_note: Ranked from most general category (chemical entity) to most specific unit (atom).

points.statement: Compound classes by composition and structure describe a substance by the kind of molecular framework it has.
points.name: Compound classes by composition and structure describe a substance by the kind of molecular framework it has.

support.rank_note: Ordered from simple inorganic to organic to ring-based frameworks.

points.statement: Biochemical substances are classes of compounds defined by the role they play in living systems.
points.name: Biochemical substances are classes of compounds defined by the role they play in living systems.

points.name: Hormones, Hormone Substitutes, and Hormone Antagonists

support.rank_note: Ranked from large macromolecules to the smaller functional biomolecules.

points.statement: Applied chemicals are substances classified by the practical use made of them in medicine and dentistry.
points.name: Applied chemicals are substances classified by the practical use made of them in medicine and dentistry.

support.rank_note: Ordered from materials to finished pharmaceutical products.

points.statement: The discipline of chemistry and its residual and forensic subfields frame the study of substances as a field of knowledge.
points.name: The discipline of chemistry and its residual and forensic subfields frame the study of substances as a field of knowledge.

points.statement: Other chemical sciences not elsewhere classified
points.name: Other chemical sciences not elsewhere classified

cells.statement: Chemistry fields are distinguished by the kind of question they ask of a substance, either about its makeup or about its behaviour.

points.statement: Composition and construction fields ask what a substance is made of, how its atoms are arranged and bonded, and how it is assembled.
points.name: Composition and construction fields ask what a substance is made of, how its atoms are arranged and bonded, and how it is assembled.

points.statement: Fields that ask which elements make up a substance and how those elements, by chemical family, behave.
points.name: Fields that ask which elements make up a substance and how those elements, by chemical family, behave.

points.statement: Fields that ask how the atoms of a substance are arranged and bonded into ordered architectures such as lattices, clusters and frameworks.
points.name: Fields that ask how the atoms of a substance are arranged and bonded into ordered architectures such as lattices, clusters and frameworks.

support.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from atomic arrangement to larger assembled frameworks.

points.statement: Fields that ask what a material or molecular assembly is made of and how its structure and internal motion are organised.
points.name: Fields that ask what a material or molecular assembly is made of and how its structure and internal motion are organised.

points.statement: Macromolecular and materials chemistry not elsewhere classified
points.name: Macromolecular and materials chemistry not elsewhere classified

support.rank_note: Ordered from elemental composition, to atomic arrangement, to formation, to residual inorganic and organised-assembly inquiries.

points.statement: Behaviour and modelling fields ask how a substance responds to light and radiation, and how its properties are designed and computed in theory.
points.name: Behaviour and modelling fields ask how a substance responds to light and radiation, and how its properties are designed and computed in theory.

points.statement: Fields that ask how a substance interacts with light and what measurable properties it displays.
points.name: Fields that ask how a substance interacts with light and what measurable properties it displays.

points.statement: Fields that ask how a material can be conceived and designed in theory to achieve desired properties, and how it behaves in aggregate.
points.name: Fields that ask how a material can be conceived and designed in theory to achieve desired properties, and how it behaves in aggregate.

points.statement: Fields that ask how a substance behaves under computation, quantum theory and its interaction with radiation.
points.name: Fields that ask how a substance behaves under computation, quantum theory and its interaction with radiation.

points.statement: Theoretical and computational chemistry not elsewhere classified
points.name: Theoretical and computational chemistry not elsewhere classified

cells.statement: The question asked of a substance is whether it changes, how it interacts and moves, or how it is observed and measured.
cells.name: The question asked of a substance is whether it changes, how it interacts and moves, or how it is observed and measured.

points.statement: Questions about change ask how a substance reacts, exchanges energy and charge, or converts from one state or form to another.
points.name: Questions about change ask how a substance reacts, exchanges energy and charge, or converts from one state or form to another.

points.statement: Questions about how a substance reacts ask by what pathway, how fast, and under what catalytic or light-driven influence a chemical change occurs.

support.rank_note: Kinds of energy and transport questions arranged by structure: energetics, electrical behaviour, solution medium, and transport processes.

field_check.governing_thought: Chemistry's objects divide by the question asked of a substance into its composition and identity, its structure and bonding, its equilibrium and energy, its rates and mechanisms, and its synthesis and analysis.
key_line: Composition and identity is the question of what a substance is, covering its general kind, role and chemical or biological class.
Structure and bonding is the question of how a substance is built, how its parts attract one another and what measurable properties follow.
Equilibrium and energy is the question of how a substance settles into states, exchanges matter and energy and moves between phases.
Rates and mechanisms is the question of how fast a substance changes and by what steps its bonds are rearranged.
Synthesis and analysis is the question of how a substance is made, isolated, detected and measured.
